chapters.title: Shelter for the Outcasts of Moab
chapters.html:
Isaiah 16

1Send the lamb to the ruler of the land,
from Sela, across the wilderness,
to the mount of the daughter of Zion.

2Like fluttering birds,
like a nest scattered,
so are the daughters of Moab
at the fords of the Arnon.

3"Give counsel;
grant a ruling;
make your shade like night
at the height of noon;
hide the outcasts;
do not betray the fugitive.

4Let the outcasts of Moab live as guests among you;
be a shelter to them from the destroyer."

When the oppressor is no more,
and destruction has ceased,
and the one who tramples has vanished from the land,

5then a throne will be established in loyal love,
and on it will sit in faithfulness,
in the tent of David,
one who judges and seeks justice
and is swift to do righteousness.

6We have heard of the pride of Moab —
how very proud he is! —
of his arrogance, his pride, and his fury;
his boasting is empty.

7So Moab wails for Moab;
all of them wail.
For the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth you will moan,
utterly stricken.

8For the fields of Heshbon languish,
and the vine of Sibmah;
the lords of the nations have struck down its choice branches,
which reached as far as Jazer
and strayed into the wilderness;
its shoots spread out
and crossed over the sea.

9So I weep with the weeping of Jazer
for the vine of Sibmah;
I drench you with my tears,
Heshbon and Elealeh;
for on your summer fruit and on your harvest
the shout has fallen.

10Joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful field;
in the vineyards no one sings,
no one shouts for joy;
no one treads out wine in the presses;
I have put an end to the shout.

11So my inner parts moan for Moab like a harp,
and my inmost being for Kir-heres.

12And it shall come to pass, when Moab presents himself, when he wears himself out on the high place and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he will not prevail.

13This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab long ago.

14But now the LORD has spoken, saying: "Within three years, like the years of a hired man, the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude, and the remnant will be very small and feeble."

Notes

  • v1 "Send the lamb to the ruler of the land" — kar, the tribute Moab once paid in lambs: Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to pay the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs (2 Kings 3:4, karim). Moab's refugees are told to send it again, now to Zion.

  • vv3–4 "Let the outcasts of Moab live as guests among you" — nidchei Mo'av, as the Greek reads it: the fugitives of Moab will live as guests with you. The Hebrew vowels read the same letters nidachai, "my outcasts," with Moab as the one spoken to: Let my outcasts live as guests among you; Moab, be a shelter to them. Read that way, Israel's outcasts ask Moab for shelter. Read the Greek's way, Moab's refugees (v2) ask the daughter of Zion (v1): most of the commands in v3 and the you of v4 are feminine, and the answer in v5 is a throne in Zion; only be in v4 is masculine. "Live as guests" — yaguru, from gur. Moab once sheltered David's family: Please let my father and my mother come and stay with you (1 Samuel 22:3).

  • v5 "a throne will be established in loyal love… in the tent of David" — chesed and emet, loyal love and faithfulness, the throne of 9:7, on the throne of David… with justice and with righteousness. The answer to the refugees is a king in Zion who judges rightly.

  • v6 "the pride of Moab… his arrogance, his pride" — ge'on, ge, ga'avato, ge'ono: four words from one root, ga'ah, "to rise up." Jeremiah 48:29 has the same line and adds more: his loftiness, his pride, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart.

  • v7 "the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth" — ashishei, pressed cakes of raisins. Jeremiah's version of the line has the men of Kir-heres (Jeremiah 48:31), and v11 here has the shorter name too. In v11 qirbi, "my inmost being," chimes with Qir.

  • v8 "the lords of the nations have struck down its choice branches" — ba'alei goyim halemu seruqqeha. The words can also be read the other way round: its choice vines struck down the lords of the nations, that is, its wine laid them low, as halumei yayin, "those struck down by wine," says of Ephraim's drunkards (28:1). The Greek reads it as rendered: the nations trample its vines.

  • vv9–10 "the shout has fallen… I have put an end to the shout" — heidad, the shout of the men treading grapes (a shout like those who tread grapes, Jeremiah 25:30). In v10 the harvest shout is silenced; in v9 a shout falls on the harvest, the enemy's.

  • v14 "like the years of a hired man" — counted to the day, no more and no less: in the law a sold man's time shall be counted like the days of a hired man (Leviticus 25:50). The same measure is set for Kedar in 21:16.

chapters.title: The Oracle Against Damascus
chapters.html:
Isaiah 17

1The oracle concerning Damascus.

Damascus is about to cease to be a city;
it will become a heap of ruins.

2The cities of Aroer are deserted;
they will be for flocks,
which will lie down with no one to make them afraid.

3The fortress will vanish from Ephraim,
and the kingdom from Damascus;
and the remnant of Aram will be
like the glory of the sons of Israel,
declares the LORD of hosts.

4And it shall come to pass in that day,
that the glory of Jacob will be brought low,
and the fat of his flesh will grow lean.

5It will be as when the reaper gathers the standing grain,
and his arm harvests the ears,
and as when one gleans the ears of grain
in the Valley of Rephaim.

6Gleanings will be left in it,
as when an olive tree is beaten:
two or three berries
at the top of the highest bough,
four or five
on the branches of a fruitful tree,
declares the LORD, the God of Israel.

7In that day man will look to his Maker,
and his eyes will look to the Holy One of Israel.

8He will not look to the altars,
the work of his hands,
and he will not look at what his fingers have made,
the Asherim and the incense altars.

9In that day his strong cities will be
like the deserted places of the woods and the hilltops,
which they deserted before the sons of Israel;
and there will be desolation.

10For you have forgotten the God of your deliverance,
and have not remembered the Rock of your stronghold;
so you plant pleasant plants,
and set them out with a stranger's vine-slips.

11On the day you plant them, you make them grow,
and in the morning you make your seed blossom;
yet the harvest will be a heap
on the day of possession,
and the pain past cure.

12Woe! The uproar of many peoples —
they roar like the roaring seas;
the thunder of nations —
they thunder like mighty waters!

13The nations thunder like the thunder of many waters,
but He rebukes them, and they flee far away,
chased like chaff on the mountains before the wind,
like whirling dust before the storm.

14At evening, sudden terror;
before morning, they are gone.
This is the portion of those who plunder us,
the lot of those who rob us.

Notes

  • vv1–3 "Damascus… Ephraim" — the two kingdoms that marched on Jerusalem together in 7:1–9, Aram with its capital Damascus and Ephraim, the northern kingdom of Israel. They fall together. "The remnant of Aram will be like the glory of the sons of Israel": like a glory that is fading (v4).

  • v4 "the fat of his flesh will grow lean" — mishman… yerazeh, the two words of 10:16, where the LORD sends leanness among his fat ones, Assyria's. Now the same wasting comes on Jacob.

  • v5 "the Valley of Rephaim" — near Jerusalem, where the Philistines came up against David (2 Samuel 5:18, 22). Its name is the word for the shades of the dead in 14:9, repha'im.

  • v6 "Gleanings will be left in it, as when an olive tree is beaten" — olelot, what the law left on the tree and the vine for the poor: When you beat your olive trees, you shall not go over the branches after you. It shall be for the guest, the orphan and the widow (Deuteronomy 24:20–21). Israel's remnant is the few olives left at the top. The picture returns in 24:13.

  • vv7–8 "his Maker… what his fingers have made" — osehu and asu, the same verb, asah, "to make." Man will look to the One who made him, not to what he made.

  • v9 "the deserted places of the woods and the hilltops, which they deserted before the sons of Israel" — the Greek reads different words: as the Amorites and the Hivites deserted them before the sons of Israel, naming the peoples of the land who left their cities when Israel came in. The Hebrew's amir, "hilltop," is the word for the top of the highest bough in v6, where the last olives hang.

  • vv9–10 "his strong cities… the Rock of your stronghold" — ma'uzzo and ma'uzzekh, the same word. Her strongholds are deserted because she forgot the Rock who was her stronghold. "The God of your deliverance" — yish'ekh, from the root of yeshu'ah in 12:2–3.

  • v11 "the harvest will be a heap on the day of possession" — ned qatsir be-yom nachalah. Ned is a heap, a standing mass, the word for the waters that stood like a wall at the sea (Exodus 15:8). Nachalah is "possession, inheritance," as the Greek also reads it; with other vowels the line reads the harvest flees in a day of sickness. The line is uncertain; either way, the plants that grew in a day bring their planter pain past cure.

  • vv12–14 "before morning, they are gone" — the nations roar like the sea, and one rebuke scatters them overnight. Isaiah tells the night it happened to Assyria's army: the messenger of the LORD went out and struck down a hundred and eighty-five thousand in the camp of Assyria; and when people rose early in the morning, there were all the dead bodies (37:36). "Like whirling dust… like chaff" — the prayer of Psalm 83:13, make them like whirling dust, like chaff before the wind.

chapters.title: A Gift from Beyond the Rivers of Cush
chapters.html:
Isaiah 18

1Woe to the land of whirring wings
beyond the rivers of Cush,

2which sends envoys by the sea,
in vessels of papyrus on the waters!
Go, swift messengers,
to a nation tall and smooth,
to a people feared near and far,
a nation of line upon line, that tramples down,
whose land the rivers divide.

3All you who live in the world,
you who dwell on the earth,
when a signal is raised on the mountains, you will see it;
when the ram's horn is blown, you will hear it.

4For thus the LORD said to me:
"I will be still and look on from My dwelling place,
like shimmering heat in the sunlight,
like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest."

5For before the harvest, when the blossom is over
and the flower becomes a ripening grape,
He will cut off the shoots with pruning hooks,
and the spreading branches He will lop off and clear away.

6They will all be left to the birds of prey of the mountains
and to the beasts of the earth;
the birds of prey will summer on them,
and all the beasts of the earth will winter on them.

7At that time a gift will be brought to the LORD of hosts — a people tall and smooth — and from a people feared near and far, a nation of line upon line, that tramples down, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, Mount Zion.

Notes

  • v1 "beyond the rivers of Cush" — Cush is the land the Greek calls Aithiopia, Ethiopia, here and in every verse of Isaiah that names it (Tirhakah king of Cush, 37:9). Its river is the Gihon of Eden, the one winding through all the land of Cush (Genesis 2:13). "Whirring wings" — tsiltsal, a word for whirring or buzzing, the cricket of Deuteronomy 28:42; the Greek reads the wings of ships, their sails.

  • v2 "vessels of papyrus" — kelei gome, the reed of the basket of papyrus in which Moses was set on the Nile (Exodus 2:3).

  • vv2, 7 "a nation of line upon line" — goy qav-qav, the doubled word for a measuring line. It comes again in 28:10, 13, qav la-qav, "line upon line," of a speech Israel will hear with stammering lips and another tongue (28:11). What it says of this nation is not known: one that measures out lands, one strong beyond measure, or one whose speech sounds to Israel like a babble. "Whose land the rivers divide" — bazu, a word found only here and in v7.

  • vv3–6 "I will be still and look on" — the LORD waits like the summer heat and the dew that ripen the crop, and then, before the harvest, cuts the shoots. Mazmerot, "pruning hooks," are what the spears are beaten into in 2:4.

  • v7 "a gift will be brought to the LORD of hosts — a people tall and smooth" — the Hebrew has no from before the first people, only before the second (and from a people feared); as written, the people themselves are the gift. The Greek has from a people both times, and most English supplies it. Isaiah ends with the nations bringing Israel's scattered brothers as an offering to the LORD… to My holy mountain Jerusalem (66:20). Kings will bring You gifts, shai, the word here (Psalm 68:29); Cush will run to stretch out its hands to God (68:31). In Acts an Ethiopian, an official of the queen of the Ethiopians, had come to Jerusalem to worship (Acts 8:27).

chapters.title: The Oracle Against Egypt
chapters.html:
Isaiah 19

1The oracle concerning Egypt.

The LORD is riding on a swift cloud
and is coming to Egypt;
the idols of Egypt tremble before Him,
and the heart of Egypt melts within it.

2"I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians,
and they will fight, each against his brother
and each against his neighbor,
city against city, kingdom against kingdom.

3The spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it,
and I will swallow up its counsel;
they will consult the idols and the whisperers,
the ghosts and the spirits.

4I will hand Egypt over
to a hard master,
and a fierce king will rule over them,"
declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.

5The waters of the sea will dry up,
and the river will be parched and dry;

6the canals will stink;
the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up;
reed and rush will wither.

7The bare places by the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile,
and everything sown by the Nile
will dry up, be driven away, and be gone.

8The fishermen will mourn and lament,
all who cast a hook into the Nile;
those who spread nets on the water will languish.

9Those who work combed flax will be ashamed,
and the weavers of white cloth.

10Its foundations will be crushed,
and all who work for wages will be grieved in soul.

11The princes of Zoan are nothing but fools;
the wisest of Pharaoh's counselors give senseless counsel.
How can you say to Pharaoh,
"I am a son of the wise,
a son of ancient kings"?

12Where then are your wise men?
Let them tell you
and make known what the LORD of hosts
has planned against Egypt.

13The princes of Zoan have become fools;
the princes of Memphis are deceived;
those who are the cornerstone of its tribes
have led Egypt astray.

14The LORD has mixed within her
a spirit of confusion,
and they have led Egypt astray in all it does,
as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.

15There will be nothing Egypt can do,
head or tail, palm branch or reed.

Egypt, My People

16In that day Egypt will be like women, and will tremble with fear before the hand that the LORD of hosts shakes over it.

17The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone to whom it is mentioned will be afraid, because of what the LORD of hosts has planned against it.

18In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.

19In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a standing stone to the LORD at its border.

20It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of those who crush them, He will send them a deliverer and a defender, and he will rescue them.

21The LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and Egypt will know the LORD in that day; they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and make vows to the LORD and keep them.

22The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing; they will return to the LORD, and He will hear their pleas and heal them.

23In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; Assyria will come into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and Egypt will worship with Assyria.

24In that day Israel will be the third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth,

25whom the LORD of hosts has blessed, saying: "Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance."

Notes

  • v1 "The LORD is riding on a swift cloud" — the LORD comes to Egypt Himself, and the land's gods and its heart give way. "The heart of Egypt melts" — yimmas, the verb used of Canaan's heart when Israel came (our hearts melted, Joshua 2:11).

  • v4 "a hard master" — adonim qasheh. Qasheh, "hard," is the word of the hard service Egypt laid on Israel (Exodus 1:14). Now Egypt is handed to a hard master.

  • v15 "head or tail, palm branch or reed" — the words of 9:14, where the LORD cut them off from Israel. Here Egypt has no one, high or low, who can do anything.

  • v18 "the City of Destruction" — ir ha-heres. Heres is "tearing down," the verb of the command to Israel about the gods of Canaan: You shall utterly tear them down and utterly break their standing stones (Exodus 23:24); read so, it is the city where the idols are torn down. The Greek has polis asedek, "the City of Righteousness," the name given Jerusalem in 1:26.

  • v19 "a standing stone to the LORD" — matsevah, what the law forbade in Israel: You shall not set up for yourself a standing stone, which the LORD your God hates (Deuteronomy 16:22). In Egypt one stands at the border, for the LORD.

  • vv20–22 "because of those who crush them… Egypt will know the LORD… striking and healing" — the exodus told in reverse. Israel cried out because of the crushing with which Egypt is crushing them (Exodus 3:9, lachats); now Egypt cries out because of lochatsim, "those who crush," and the LORD sends a deliverer, as He did for Israel in Judges (the LORD raised up a deliverer, Judges 3:9). Egypt will know that I am the LORD (Exodus 7:5) was said of the plagues; here it is said of worship. Nagaf, "strike," is the verb of the last plague (the LORD will pass through to strike Egypt, Exodus 12:23), and here the stroke is followed by healing, as I am the LORD your healer was promised Israel (Exodus 15:26).

  • vv24–25 "Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance" — ammi, "My people," the name the LORD gave Israel when He sent Moses to Pharaoh (Exodus 3:7), is given to Egypt, and Israel is the third, a blessing in the middle of the earth, as Abraham was told, In you all the families of the ground shall be blessed (Genesis 12:3). The Greek softens it: Blessed be My people who are in Egypt and who are among the Assyrians.

speech.text: Isaiah 19
The oracle concerning Egypt. The LORD is riding on a swift cloud and is coming to Egypt; the idols of Egypt tremble before Him, and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
"I will stir up Egyptians against Egyptians, and they will fight, each against his brother and each against his neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, and I will swallow up its counsel; they will consult the idols and the whisperers, the ghosts and the spirits.
I will hand Egypt over to a hard master, and a fierce king will rule over them," declares the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
The waters of the sea will dry up, and the river will be parched and dry;
the canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up; reed and rush will wither.
The bare places by the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and everything sown by the Nile will dry up, be driven away, and be gone.
The fishermen will mourn and lament, all who cast a hook into the Nile; those who spread nets on the water will languish.
Those who work combed flax will be ashamed, and the weavers of white cloth.
Its foundations will be crushed, and all who work for wages will be grieved in soul.
The princes of Zoan are nothing but fools; the wisest of Pharaoh's counselors give senseless counsel. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings"?
Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you and make known what the LORD of hosts has planned against Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools; the princes of Memphis are deceived; those who are the cornerstone of its tribes have led Egypt astray.
The LORD has mixed within her a spirit of confusion, and they have led Egypt astray in all it does, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
There will be nothing Egypt can do, head or tail, palm branch or reed.
Egypt, My People
In that day Egypt will be like women, and will tremble with fear before the hand that the LORD of hosts shakes over it.
The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt; everyone to whom it is mentioned will be afraid, because of what the LORD of hosts has planned against it.
In that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.
In that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a standing stone to the LORD at its border.

It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of those who crush them, He will send them a deliverer and a defender, and he will rescue them.
The LORD will make Himself known to Egypt, and Egypt will know the LORD in that day; they will worship with sacrifice and offering, and make vows to the LORD and keep them.
The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing; they will return to the LORD, and He will hear their pleas and heal them.
In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; Assyria will come into Egypt, and Egypt into Assyria, and Egypt will worship with Assyria.
In that day Israel will be the third with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth,
whom the LORD of hosts has blessed, saying: "Blessed be Egypt My people, and Assyria the work of My hands, and Israel My inheritance."

chapters.title: Naked and Barefoot
chapters.html:
Isaiah 20

1In the year that the commander in chief came to Ashdod, when Sargon king of Assyria sent him, and he fought against Ashdod and took it,

2at that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz, saying, "Go, loosen the sackcloth from your waist and take your sandals off your feet." He did so, walking naked and barefoot.

3The LORD said, "As My servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush,

4so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks uncovered, the nakedness of Egypt.

5They will be dismayed and ashamed because of Cush, whom they looked to, and Egypt, their boast.

6In that day the inhabitants of this coastland will say, 'This is what has become of the one we looked to, to whom we fled for help, to be rescued from the king of Assyria! How then will we escape?'"

Notes

  • v1 "the commander in chief… Sargon king of Assyria" — tartan, the title of an Assyrian officer, the one sent with others to Jerusalem in 2 Kings 18:17. Sargon is named nowhere else in the Bible. The Greek has neither name right (Tanathan… Arna).

  • v2 "spoke through Isaiah" — be-yad, literally "by the hand of": the message is the act. Isaiah says nothing in this chapter; for three years he walks, and the walking is the word.

  • v3 "a sign and a portent" — ot u-mofet, the words of 8:18, Here am I and the children the LORD has given me, as signs and portents in Israel. Isaiah himself is now one.

  • vv5–6 "Cush, whom they looked to… the one we looked to" — mabbat, "what one looks to," twice: the people of the coast had looked to Egypt and Cush, the powers of the Nile, against Assyria, and they watch them led away naked. Isaiah 18 and 19 have just spoken of those two lands; here the hope placed in them is ended.

chapters.title: Fallen, Fallen Is Babylon
chapters.html:
Isaiah 21

1The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea.

Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev,
it comes from the wilderness,
from a terrible land.

2A hard vision has been told to me:
the traitor betrays,
and the destroyer destroys.
Go up, Elam!
Lay siege, Media!
All the sighing she caused
I bring to an end.

3So my loins are filled with anguish;
pangs have seized me,
like the pangs of a woman in labor;
I am bent double at what I hear;
I am terrified at what I see.

4My heart staggers;
horror has overwhelmed me;
the twilight I longed for
has been turned to trembling for me.

5They set the table,
they spread the rugs,
they eat, they drink.
Rise up, commanders;
anoint the shield!

6For thus the Lord said to me:
"Go, post a watchman;
let him report what he sees.

7When he sees riders,
horsemen in pairs,
riders on donkeys,
riders on camels,
let him listen closely,
very closely."

8Then he cried out like a lion:
"On the watchtower, Lord,
I stand continually by day,
and at my post I am stationed
every night.

9Here comes a man in a chariot,
with horsemen in pairs!"
Then he answered:
"Fallen, fallen is Babylon,
and all the carved images of her gods
He has shattered to the ground."

10My threshed one, the grain of my threshing floor,
what I have heard from the LORD of hosts,
the God of Israel,
I have told you.

Dumah

11The oracle concerning Dumah.

One calls to me from Seir:
"Watchman, what of the night?
Watchman, what of the night?"

12The watchman says:
"Morning comes, and also the night.
If you would ask, ask;
come back again."

Arabia

13The oracle concerning Arabia.

In the thickets of Arabia you will spend the night,
you caravans of Dedanites.

14To the thirsty bring water,
you who live in the land of Tema;
meet the fugitive with bread.

15For they have fled from the swords,
from the drawn sword,
from the bent bow,
and from the weight of battle.

16For thus the Lord said to me: "Within a year, like the years of a hired man, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end;

17and the remnant of the archers, the mighty men of the sons of Kedar, will be few; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken."

Notes

  • v1 "the wilderness of the sea" — a riddling name; v9 says what it is: Babylon. "Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media!" (v2): the Medes, named in 13:17 as the power that takes Babylon, with Elam beside them.

  • v5 "They set the table… they eat, they drink. Rise up, commanders" — a feast broken by a call to arms. Daniel tells Babylon's last night in the same way: Belshazzar's feast, and that very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed (Daniel 5:1, 30). "Spread the rugs" — tsafoh ha-tsafit; tsafit is found only here. The verb tsafah is also "to watch," the root of watchman (v6) and watchtower (v8), and read so the line is keep the watch. The Greek has only Prepare the table, eat, drink. "Anoint the shield" — mishchu, the verb of anointing: leather shields were rubbed with oil, and Saul's was no longer anointed with oil (2 Samuel 1:21).

  • v8 "he cried out like a lion" — va-yiqra aryeh, literally "he cried, a lion." Who cries, and why a lion, is not clear: the watchman shouting with a lion's voice is the plain reading. The Greek reads different words, call Uriah to the watchtower.

  • v9 "Fallen, fallen is Babylon" — nafelah nafelah Bavel. Revelation takes up the cry twice, Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great (Revelation 14:8; 18:2).

  • v10 "My threshed one, the grain of my threshing floor" — medushati u-ven gorni, literally "my threshed one and son of my threshing floor": the prophet's own people, beaten on the floor like grain, are the ones he tells.

  • vv11–12 "Dumah… Seir" — Seir is Edom's mountain (Genesis 36:8), and dumah is "silence" (my soul would soon have dwelt in silence, Psalm 94:17). The watchman's answer is in words close to Aramaic, tiv'ayun… be'ayu… eteyu, "ask… come": morning comes, but night as well; they may come back and ask again.

  • vv16–17 "like the years of a hired man" — the measure set for Moab in 16:14: counted exactly, no more. Kedar is one of Ishmael's sons (Genesis 25:13).

chapters.title: The Key of the House of David
chapters.html:
Isaiah 22

1The oracle concerning the Valley of Vision.

What is the matter with you,
that you have all gone up to the housetops,

2you who are full of shouting,
a tumultuous city, an exultant town?
Your slain were not slain by the sword,
nor did they die in battle.

3All your rulers fled together;
without a bow they were captured.
All of you who were found were captured together,
though they had fled far away.

4So I said: "Look away from me;
let me weep bitterly;
do not try to comfort me
over the destruction of the daughter of my people."

5For the Lord GOD of hosts has a day
of tumult and trampling and confusion
in the Valley of Vision,
a battering down of walls
and a crying out to the mountain.

6Elam took up the quiver,
with chariots of men and horsemen,
and Kir bared the shield.

7Your choicest valleys were full of chariots,
and the horsemen took their stand at the gate.

8He stripped away the covering of Judah.

In that day you looked to the weapons of the House of the Forest,

9and you saw that the breaches in the City of David were many. You collected the waters of the lower pool,

10and you counted the houses of Jerusalem, and tore down the houses to fortify the wall.

11You made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to Him who did it, or see Him who planned it long ago.

12In that day the Lord GOD of hosts called
for weeping and mourning,
for baldness and putting on sackcloth;

13but instead there was joy and gladness,
killing oxen and slaughtering sheep,
eating meat and drinking wine:
"Let us eat and drink,
for tomorrow we die."

14The LORD of hosts has revealed Himself in my hearing: "Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you until you die," says the Lord GOD of hosts.

Shebna and Eliakim

15Thus says the Lord GOD of hosts: "Go, come to this steward, to Shebna, who is over the household, and say:

16'What have you here, and whom have you here, that you have cut out a tomb for yourself here — cutting out his tomb on the height, carving a dwelling for himself in the rock?

17The LORD is about to hurl you away, hurl you, you strong man, and grip you hard;

18He will wind you round and round and throw you like a ball into a wide land. There you will die, and there will be your splendid chariots, you disgrace to your master's house.

19I will thrust you from your office, and from your post he will pull you down.

20And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call My servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah,

21and I will clothe him with your robe, and bind your sash on him, and put your authority in his hand; and he will be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.

22I will set the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open, and no one will shut; he will shut, and no one will open.

23I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a throne of honor for his father's house.

24They will hang on him the whole weight of his father's house, the offspring and the offshoots, every small vessel, from the bowls to all the jars.

25In that day, declares the LORD of hosts, the peg that was driven into a firm place will give way; it will be cut down and fall, and the load that was on it will be cut off, for the LORD has spoken.'"

Notes

  • v1 "the Valley of Vision" — the oracles on the nations come home: this one is against Jerusalem itself (vv9–10), the place of Isaiah's visions. The city is on its rooftops, celebrating, while the prophet weeps (v4).

  • vv5–6 "a battering down of walls… and Kir bared the shield" — meqarqar qir, "a tearing down of walls," and then Qir, the land of Kir: the same sound, the wall and the people who come to break it.

  • vv8–11 "you looked to the weapons… you did not look to Him who did it" — va-tabbet and lo hibbattem, the same verb, nabat, "look to." They looked to the armory of the House of the Forest (Solomon's House of the Forest of Lebanon, where he put his gold shields, 1 Kings 7:2; 10:17), counted houses, collected water, built up the wall, the work Hezekiah did against Assyria (to stop the water of the springs… built up all the wall that was broken down, 2 Chronicles 32:3–5). What they did not look to was the One who made it all, as in 17:7, man will look to his Maker.

  • v13 "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die" — Paul quotes it in the Greek, of those who deny the resurrection: if the dead are not raised, Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die (1 Corinthians 15:32).

  • v14 "Surely this iniquity will not be atoned for you" — yekhuppar, the word spoken over Isaiah's own lips, your sin is atoned for (6:7). The coal was given to him; to the feasting city the same word is refused.

  • vv15, 20 "Shebna, who is over the household… My servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah" — al ha-bayit, the title of the king's chief steward (1 Kings 4:6). When Assyria comes to Jerusalem's walls, it is Eliakim son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, who goes out, and Shebna the secretary with him (36:3): the office has passed as this chapter says.

  • v22 "the key of the house of David on his shoulder; he will open, and no one will shut" — al shikhmo, the words of 9:6, the government shall be on his shoulder. Revelation gives the line to Christ: the Holy One, the True One, who has the key of David, who opens and no one will shut (Revelation 3:7).

  • vv23–25 "a throne of honor… the whole weight of his father's house… the load" — kavod, "honor," is also "weight": the peg is made a seat of honor, and the family hangs its whole weight on it until it gives way. Ha-massa, "the load," is the word the chapter opened with, the oracle; the burden laid on the peg falls with it.
